reason: E1 and E2 show coherent precipitates improve strength and ductility in a W-based HEA, but do not address radiation tolerance. E4 shows TiC can form in a W–Ta–Ti–V–Cr system via SPS, but does not test radiation effects. E3 demonstrates that alloy complexity enhances radiation tolerance via defect recombination, but in Ni-based alloys, not W-based HEAs with precipitates. The key premise that coherent TiC interfaces will act as radiation defect sinks is not directly supported by any cited evidence, and the combined effect on mechanical properties under irradiation is untested.
premises: Coherent nanoscale precipitates in W-based HEAs can simultaneously provide high strength and ductility
TiC can be introduced in-situ in W-based HEAs via spark plasma sintering
Coherent precipitate interfaces can act as effective sinks for radiation-induced defects
Alloy complexity can enhance radiation tolerance by promoting defect recombination
The specific W–Ta–Ti–V–Cr system with TiC precipitates will retain mechanical integrity under irradiation at ~800 °C
